messages:
Alex: Heads up — we've got gRPC streaming stalls on pod-to-pod traffic in eu-west-2, looks correlated with GPU training pods across two AZs.
Maria: Observed the same. Streams hang for ~15-30s then resume, causing retries and OOMs in trainers. Repro with synthetic streamer.
Jit: Any packet drops on the wire? I ran a quick tcpdump between node-12 and node-07 while reproducing.
Jit: ```
15:42:10.123456 IP node-12 > node-07: Flags [P.], seq 12345:12800, ack 54321, win 65535, length 455
15:42:10.123789 IP node-07 > node-12: ICMP frag needed and DF set (mtu = 1452)
15:42:10.124000 IP node-12 > node-07: retransmission, seq 12345:12800, length 455
```
Tanya: ICMP "fragmentation needed" + DF set => classic PMTU issue. Why mtu=1452? Our overlay + vlan tagging math maybe.
Maria: We recently enabled Q-in-Q at the ToR for customer isolation; that adds 4 bytes per packet. CNI (calico+vxlan) uses 50 bytes overhead; default eth0 MTU 1500 -> effective path MTU 1500 - 54 = 1446? Not matching 1452 though.
Alex: Host NIC MTU is 1500, vxlan on host is set to 1450 for historical reasons on other clusters. I wonder if a middlebox is clamping to 1452 (AWS ENI + trunking?)
SRE-QA: Ran iperf3 with large packets across same nodes, shows MSS clamping and lots of retransmits. Quick check: `ip -d link show vxlan.calico` shows MTU 1450 on host but underlying interface set to 1456 after vlan tagging.
SRE-QA: ```
# on node-12
$ ip link show eth0
eth0 mtu 1456 qdisc mq state UP
$ ip link show vxlan.calico
vxlan.calico mtu 1450 qdisc noop state UNKNOWN
```
Jit: So mismatch: underlay 1456 vs overlay 1450 => PMTU discovery negotiating to 1452 somewhere in path. gRPC streaming uses large messages (protobuf chunks ~16k) with TCP DF set — when path can't handle it, ICMP returned but maybe filtered by security group -> blackholing.
Maria: Yep, some AWS ENI health rules drop ICMP in our accounts (legacy security template). If ICMP blocked, PMTU fails and you get persistent stalls/retransmits.
Tanya: Impact: about 20% of GPU streaming jobs experience multi-second stalls, increasing GPU idle time and pushing provisioned capacity up because jobs retry. Seen 8% P99 latency spike in inference streaming too.
Alex: Temporary mitigation: reduce overlay MTU across cluster to 1400 so all encapsulations fit. Also enable `net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` on hosts to allow opportunistic MTU discovery.
Maria: Commands I pushed to a DaemonSet (testing):
```
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1
ip link set vxlan.calico mtu 1400
```
Jit: For a stable fix we should: 1) audit ToR/ENI trunking for extra tag bytes and set consistent MTU 2) align CNI overlay MTU with underlay MTU - overhead 50-60 bytes 3) update security groups to allow ICMP Type 3 Code 4 (Fragmentation needed)
SRE-QA: Also consider reducing gRPC max message size or enable chunked smaller writes in training pipeline to avoid single huge TCP segments.
Tanya: Note for RDMA / RoCE flows on GPU nodes — we can't just shrink MTU arbitrarily; RDMA wants consistent jumbo frames (e.g., 9000). Those nodes are in same AZ so we can steer RDMA traffic on non-encapsulated path.
Alex: Plan proposal:
- Roll cluster-wide overlay MTU -> 1400 (immediate mitigation) [ops playbook]
- Submit ticket to network infra to remove unexpected VLAN Q-in-Q on affected ToRs or set trunk MTU to 9000 if we want jumbo everywhere
- Patch security group templates to allow PMTU ICMP replies
- Add tcp_mtu_probing sysctl in node bootstrap
- Add e2e test in perf suite to detect PMTU blackholes (iperf, tcpdump pattern)
Maria: I'm on the playbook for the DaemonSet change and can push a canary to eu-west-2a first.
Jit: I'll open a network ticket with packet captures attached and point to the ToR configs we saw.
OpsBot: Incident created: INC-2026-1987 by Jit — linked to gpu-fleet-impact. Assigned to net-infra.
Alex: Thanks. After mitigation we should monitor P99 stream latency and GPU utilization; mark this as Sev3 until fixed across AZs.
SRE-QA: I'll add a dashboard alert for ICMP frag-needed rate and gRPC stream stalls.
Maria: Can we also add a note in runbook about RDMA-aware MTU config so we don't break RoCE when changing overlay MTU?
